back: Sensible, valid data that should be accepted and processed correctly.
Data that should be rejected: out of range or the wrong type (also called erroneous data).
The largest and smallest values that are still accepted.
A pair either side of a limit: the last accepted value and the first rejected value (e.g. 10 and 11 for 1 to 10).
Finds off-by-one errors such as < used instead of <=, which only show at the limits.
Table of tests: number, purpose, test data, type, expected result; actual result added when run.
Expected is decided from the requirements before testing; a different actual result shows an error.
The first rejected value depends on precision: for two decimal places, the value next to 99.99 is 100.00.
